Subject: Request: temporary quarterly invoicing + extended payment terms

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team at Cumulus is very excited about Redwood's latency profile and observability features. We're close to a procurement decision, but we ran the numbers against a new grant schedule and have a short-term treasury constraint.

Two asks from our side to close this quarter:
- Move to quarterly invoicing for the first two billing cycles (helps align with grant disbursements).
- Accept Net-90 payment terms for the first 6 months (we can convert back to standard monthly Net-30 after that).

Attached is a mutual action plan and a draft SOW to speed legal review. If Redwood can approve these temporary terms, we can commit to a 12-month contract (volume: ~3.5M tokens/month initially) and a signed SOW within 10 business days.

Are these terms you can escalate? Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the timing — Tom (cc'd) is our finance lead.

Best,
Alicia Chen
Director of Procurement
Cumulus Health

Attachments: Cumulus_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), cumulus-draft-sow.pdf (pdf)

Thanks, Alicia — appreciate the clear asks and the MAP. I can escalate. Per our intake checklist, I'll need internal signoff on:
1) Temporary invoicing cadence (quarterly for two cycles)
2) Extended payment terms (Net-90 for 6 months)
3) Any commercial concession tied to those terms (we usually ask for a short-term consideration or minimum commitment)

Monica / Neha — looping you in for deal desk/finance input. Customer is willing to sign a 12-month contract and provide a PO; they'd like us to confirm within 72 hours.

Next steps I propose: Monica to summarize recommended approval + conditional commercial, Jon (revenue) to weigh in on risk/precedent, and if approved I will confirm terms to Alicia and request a PO + signed SOW.

Sergio Alvarez

Subject: Fwd: Customer request — temporary quarterly invoicing + Net-90 (summary & recommendation)

Team, forwarding the ask from Cumulus (below). Quick summary and recommendation:

Customer: Cumulus Health (Alicia Chen / Tom Ruiz)
Ask: Two-cycle quarterly invoicing + Net-90 for first 6 months
Commitment: 12-month contract, estimated start volume ~3.5M tokens/month
Attachments: MAP + draft SOW included in original mail

Commercial risk and recommendation:
- Risk: Net-90 increases DSO and collection exposure. Quarterly invoicing amplifies cash timing mismatch.
- Mitigation: Conditional approval if customer provides either (A) a signed PO with a 25% upfront prepayment against the first quarterly invoice, OR (B) a bank-issued letter of credit covering the first two invoices.
- Term: Temporary for the first two billing cycles only. Revert to standard monthly Net-30 thereafter.

If approved, recommend we offer a one-time implementation credit equal to 8% of estimated first-quarter invoice (applied as a one-off invoice credit), in exchange for the 12-month committed term and the PO or LC above.

Approvers requested: Jonas (Revenue), Neha (Sales Ops) — please respond with approve/decline/modify. If approved, Sergio will confirm to the customer and collect PO.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive - Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the clear recommendation. Approve with the following conditions:
1) Approval window: Temporary terms are approved for the first two billing cycles only (explicit clause in SOW).
2) Commercial condition: Customer must provide a PO plus 25% prepayment against the first quarterly invoice OR submit a bank-issued LC covering both quarter invoices. No exception.
3) Credit concession: Approve the one-time 8% implementation credit subject to legal sign-off and finance marking the credit as recoverable if contract terminates within the first 6 months.
4) Reporting: Enable billing alerting in Console and add a 30/60/90 collection trigger to the account to ensure collection cadence is monitored.

Jonas Weber
VP Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
